records.title: PySceneDetect
records.summary: A Python library and CLI that finds shot boundaries in a video and can split it, save frames or write a cut list.
records.why_it_matters: Run on a render, it gives detected cut times and shot lengths (they depend on detector thresholds and minimum scene length), so a review step can check pacing and catch accidental cuts or a missing transition.
records.fit_notes: For a generated clip, run `scenedetect -i out.mp4 detect-adaptive list-scenes` and compare cut count and shot lengths with the shot list. The docs name detect-threshold, not the content detectors, for fades in/out; use it or ffmpeg blackdetect for those. Needs Python and a video backend (OpenCV by default; PyAV and MoviePy are also listed); not installed or run here.

related.note: ffmpeg scdet gives a per-frame score without splitting

claims.text: Use detect-adaptive or detect-content for hard cuts and detect-threshold for fades.
claims.quote: For [detector] use detect-adaptive or detect-content to find fast cuts, and detect-threshold for fades in/out.

claims.text: Scenes shorter than 0.6 s are not split off by default.
claims.quote: Minimum length of any scene. TIMECODE can be specified as number of frames (-m 10), time in seconds (-m 2.5), or timecode (-m 00:02:53.633). Default: 0.6s

claims.text: detect-content cuts when the frame difference score exceeds 27.0 by default.
claims.quote: Lower values are more sensitive to shot changes. Refers to “content_val” in stats file. Default: 27.0

records.title: VMAF (libvmaf)
records.summary: Netflix's full-reference perceptual video quality metric, as a C library, CLI and ffmpeg filter, with PSNR, SSIM and the CAMBI banding detector included.
records.why_it_matters: It measures what an export step lost against the master, and the phone model fits clips watched on a phone.
records.fit_notes: Full-reference only: it needs a reference (the master) and the encode at the same size and frame count, so it checks the encode, not whether a generated clip looks good. Use the phone model for 9:16 shorts. CAMBI is useful on generated gradients and skies. The v1 models date from 2026-06; an ffmpeg build may still ship v0, check the model path. Not run here.

related.note: ffmpeg libvmaf filter when built with it

claims.text: The v1 phone model assumes a viewing distance of 5 screen heights.
claims.quote: Phone Model: Derived by setting the normalized viewing distance to 5H (based on experimental data)

claims.text: A new v1 model set was released in June 2026.
claims.quote: (2026-06) We are releasing a new set of VMAF models (v1).

claims.text: libvmaf includes CAMBI, a detector for banding artefacts.
claims.quote: (2021-10-7) We are open-sourcing CAMBI (Contrast Aware Multiscale Banding Index) - Netflix's detector for banding (aka contouring) artifacts.

records.title: ttml-validator (BBC)
records.summary: A BBC command-line validator that checks EBU-TT-D subtitle files against the technical requirements of the BBC Subtitle Guidelines, and TTML2 files against the DAPT profile.
records.why_it_matters: It is a first-party linter for the BBC rules, so an agent can check a subtitle file without re-implementing the guidelines.
records.fit_notes: Only TTML input (EBU-TT-D or DAPT); SRT and VTT need converting first, and most short-form tools emit SRT or VTT. It checks technical rules only, so reading rate and line breaks still need a separate check. Built with Python 3.14, which the README suggests having available; setup uses poetry or uv. Not installed or run here.

claims.text: It checks EBU-TT-D files against the BBC guidelines' technical rules, not the editorial ones.
claims.quote: EBU-TT-D meeting the technical (but not editorial) requirements of the

claims.text: Its authors say technical validation does not replace previewing subtitles against the video.
claims.quote: Note that technical validation of a standalone file is not a substitute for previewing the presented file against the media it relates to
Built with python 3.14, so you might want to make sure you have that version available.
